story.title: Girls can also be doctors - Kadambini
paragraphs_en: Many many years ago when Kadambini's grandmother fell sick, the family became worried. "Baba, call a doctor immediately"...requested Kadambini. " Grandmother would not want to get treated by a man doctor."...said her father sadly. "Why don't we have girl doctors then?"...Kadambini questioned

"I will be a doctor when I grow up"...Kadambini thought. Kadambini decided to become a doctor so that she can cure women and children who do not want to go to male doctors. Kadambini read lot of books and more books. She went to school and then to college.

"Girls cannot be doctors"...people said. No one thought that girls can become a doctor. No girl in Calcutta ever thought of becoming a doctor. But Kadambini was persistent. She studied hard and harder. She became the first girl to go to the Calcutta Medical College.

Kadambini was the only girl in her class at Calcutta Medical College. She was the first girl in Calcutta to become a doctor to be able to treat people. Kadambini wanted to learn more to become a better doctor. So she went to England to study more.
Kadambini returned back to the country after her study and became the doctor she had wished to be. Doctor for women and children. "Girls can also be doctors"...she said.

Kadambini Ganguly (Bose) was born in Bhagalpur British India on July 18, 1861. Kadambini attended India's first college for women, the Bethune College in Calcutta. The first classes consisted of only two girl students, Kadambini and her friend Chandramukhi Basu.They completed their studies in 1883, becoming the first women to graduate college in India.

Kadambini then studied harder to become a doctor. She was the first girl in India to study at Calcutta Medical College. She graduated in 1886 with a Graduate of Bengal Medical College Degree, becoming the pioneer women doctors in India along with Anandibai Joshi. Kadambini went to United Kingdom in 1892 to get more experience in her field and received various certificates from Edinburgh, Glasgow, and Dublin. After returning to India, she became a doctor for women and children.
